content.value_statement: Curriculum teams need clear proof that skill levels progress logically. This skill maps lessons to CEFR, Bloom taxonomy, and DigComp levels with measurable indicators.
actual_capabilities: Maps skills to CEFR levels from A1 through C2.
Aligns learning tasks with Bloom taxonomy stages.
Creates measurable indicators for each proficiency level.
Checks lesson sequences for regression and missing prerequisites.
Suggests assessment formats that match target proficiency.
Uses reference guidance for CEFR, Bloom taxonomy, DigComp, and cognitive load.
limitations: It depends on accurate lesson goals and learner context from the user.
It does not replace validation by qualified curriculum experts.
It does not collect learner performance data or run analytics.
It uses included reference material, not live standards updates.

use_cases.title: Design Lesson Skill Maps
use_cases.description: Map each lesson skill to a target proficiency level and measurable student behavior.

use_cases.title: Audit Curriculum Progression
use_cases.description: Find proficiency regressions, missing prerequisites, and isolated skills across a course outline.

use_cases.title: Build Assessment Rubrics
use_cases.description: Create assessment criteria that distinguish recognition, application, analysis, and evaluation.

prompt_templates.title: Map One Skill
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner mapping for a single lesson objective.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the skills-proficiency-mapper skill. Map this lesson skill to CEFR and Bloom levels, then give measurable indicators: [skill and lesson context].

prompt_templates.title: Check A Lesson Sequence
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of several connected lessons.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the skills-proficiency-mapper skill. Review these lesson skills for level progression, prerequisites, and cognitive load: [lesson sequence].

prompt_templates.title: Design Matching Assessments
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced assessment design for target proficiency levels.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the skills-proficiency-mapper skill. Create assessment tasks and rubric criteria for these target levels: [skills, levels, learner profile].

prompt_templates.title: Audit A Curriculum Map
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review across chapters or modules.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the skills-proficiency-mapper skill. Audit this curriculum map for duplicated skill names, regressions, missing foundations, and isolated skills: [curriculum map].

output_examples.input: Map a lesson where students write a project specification from a short product brief.
output_examples.output: The skill fits B1 and Apply. Students independently create a complete specification, identify required details, and explain why each requirement matters.

output_examples.input: Review a sequence with A2 specification writing followed by A1 requirement recognition.
output_examples.output: The sequence regresses. Teach recognition first, then simple specification writing, then independent specification design in a later lesson.

output_examples.input: Create assessment guidance for a B2 skill about comparing specification approaches.
output_examples.output: Use a comparative analysis task. Ask learners to evaluate tradeoffs, defend criteria, and recommend an approach for a realistic project context.

best_practices: Provide lesson objectives, learner background, available time, and prerequisite knowledge.
Ask for measurable indicators before asking for assessments.
Review proposed levels against real learner work and domain expert judgment.
anti_patterns: Do not assign levels from vague difficulty labels alone.
Do not skip prerequisite checks when mapping advanced skills.
Do not use one assessment type for every proficiency level.

faq.question: What frameworks does this skill use?
faq.answer: It uses CEFR, Bloom taxonomy, DigComp, cognitive load guidance, and skill progression checks.

faq.question: Can it map technical skills?
faq.answer: Yes. It can map coding, specification, digital, and professional skills when given clear lesson context.

faq.question: Does it create complete courses?
faq.answer: No. It supports proficiency mapping, coherence checks, and assessment alignment for provided course plans.

faq.question: How much input should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide the skill name, lesson objective, learner level, prerequisites, time available, and target outcome.

faq.question: Can it detect broken progression?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks for level regression, missing prerequisites, duplicate names, and skills that never deepen.

faq.question: Is expert review still needed?
faq.answer: Yes. Use it as a structured drafting and audit tool, then validate decisions with curriculum experts.
